answer: One grove walnut-crate set per applicant: a 65-credit bond locked to its key, and a quartz tag sealed to that key on each crate, recorded once; a second return of the same tag is refused. The deposit for the k-th set is 25+6(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 6019 and 1000 fake sets cost 3,022,000 plus 65,000 locked bonds. An honest applicant pays 25 once and recovers deposit and bond when walnut crates return. An auditor checks returned tags against the grove registry and burns the bond on a missing or reused tag. A rented-tag ring fails because one quartz tag can be returned by one key.
